rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Ken Griffin says, AI is almost certainly a bubble
rows.Claim: Citadel's Ken Griffin said this week that AI is 'almost certainly' a bubble, at Citadel's Future of Global Markets conference.
rows.Evidence: Griffin made the remark at Citadel's Future of Global Markets conference in New York on 20 Oct 2026, while saying he remains bullish on AI long term and that companies are struggling to extract productivity from AI spend.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: 1% of companies represent 90% of AI spending, so that's tokens. And of that 90%, 80% of them are from unprofitable VC-backed companies
rows.Claim: 1% of companies account for 90% of AI (token) spending, and 80% of that comes from unprofitable VC-backed companies; Ramp's chief economist confirmed the estimate.
rows.Evidence: The figures originate from Chamath's own back-of-envelope post on X. Coverage of the claim cites no dataset or methodology, and the Ramp charts he referenced had not been published at recording time. Separate reporting on Ramp data points to heavy concentration of OpenAI/Anthropic spend among a small share of firms, but nothing public confirms the 90% or 80% figures.
rows.Notes: Re-check once Ramp publishes the charts Chamath previewed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: PHP, which is an open-source coding language, powers about 70% of all websites
rows.Claim: PHP powers about 70% of all websites.
rows.Evidence: Industry trackers and coverage of the PHP2Shell flaws put PHP's share at roughly 70-80% of websites whose server-side language is known.
rows.Notes: Share is of sites with a known server-side language, not literally all websites.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: In August, security researchers using AI found two, one, two critical exploits nicknamed PHP to shell. PHP security team gave this a severity rating of 9.2 out of 10
rows.Claim: PHP2Shell: two critical flaws found in August by researchers using AI, rated 9.2/10; a coordinated patch planned for 22 Oct was moved up a day after details leaked; European governments took sites offline.
rows.Evidence: Wiz found the first flaw on 19 Aug 2026 using AI-assisted research and reported both to PHP on 24 Aug; both CVEs are rated 9.2 (CVSS v4.0). Details leaked hours before disclosure and PHP shipped fixes on 21 Oct, ahead of the planned date. Government sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Finland, France and Germany went offline. Amazon saw exploitation attempts from 17 Oct.
rows.Notes: Minor details not confirmed: Denmark taking sites down, Wikipedia outages, Cloudflare 'millions' of attempts, NSA warning (FBI and CISA warnings confirmed).

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Over half a million people have taken part in the protests. They've now spread to Italy, Spain, Albania
rows.Claim: French protests drew over half a million people and spread to Italy, Spain and Albania; over 1,000 police injured, 2,500 arrested, and a 143-year-old city hall burned.
rows.Evidence: About 550,000 people protested nationwide on 17 Oct; the interior ministry reported nearly 2,400 arrests and almost 1,000 police and gendarmes injured. Limoges' 143-year-old town hall was gutted by fire. Protests were also reported in Italy, Spain, Portugal, Belgium and Albania.
rows.Notes: Jason's town name ('Le Mauge') is a transcription of Limoges.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Over 3,000 businesses, Chamath, have been damaged
rows.Claim: Over 3,000 businesses have been damaged in the French riots.
rows.Evidence: The latest figure found is from a French retail trade group, which put damaged shops and retailers at about 1,500 as of 18 Oct. No source located for 3,000.
rows.Notes: Jason attributed his figures to the New York Times; check whether a later count reached 3,000.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: France's tenure has surpassed 5% this week, highest since 2002
rows.Claim: France's 10-year bond yield surpassed 5% this week, the highest since 2002.
rows.Evidence: France's 10-year yield topped 5% on 21 Oct 2026 and reached 5.05% on 22 Oct, the highest since mid-2002.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: It's already proposed 50 billion euros of austerity
rows.Claim: France's government has already proposed about €50 billion of austerity.
rows.Evidence: PM Sébastien Lecornu presented a 2027 budget with a €54 billion savings effort on 17 Sep 2026.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: I think they are going to lose the upcoming presidential elections
rows.Claim: The current French governing camp will lose the 2027 presidential election.
rows.Evidence: The election is scheduled for 18 April (first round) and 2 May 2027 (second round). Rule (signed off 28 Oct): the government candidate is whoever Macron's Renaissance party or the governing coalition formally backs in the first round; Accurate if that candidate does not win.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: you can see the comparison of France's public spending as a percent of GDP to the peak public spending as a percent of GDP of major communist nations
rows.Claim: France's public spending as a share of GDP exceeds the peak levels of major communist states, including the Soviet Union in 1989, communist Romania, Chavez's Venezuela and communist China.
rows.Evidence: The raw numbers roughly hold: French public spending was 57.2% of GDP in 2025, and the Soviet state budget was about 51% of GDP in 1989. But the comparison is apples to oranges. In planned economies the state owned virtually all enterprises, so most economic activity sat outside the budget figure, and those budgets understate state control of the economy.
rows.Notes: Friedberg presented a chart he attributed to 'RAND Group Research'; the original chart was not located.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: France spends more than every other communist government in the history of the world
rows.Claim: France spends more than every communist government in history, roughly twice as much as communist China.
rows.Evidence: Same issue as the chart Friedberg showed: French public spending (57.2% of GDP) is higher than the Soviet state budget share (about 51% in 1989), but headline budgets of communist states exclude the state-owned enterprise sector, so the comparison understates how much of those economies the state controlled.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: Federal government spending is 7.4 trillion
rows.Claim: US federal government spending is $7.4 trillion.
rows.Evidence: CBO reports FY2026 federal outlays of $7.4 trillion.
rows.Notes: His follow-on 36% of GDP total adds state and local spending, which double-counts federal grants to states; not rated here.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: France today is the same as the US. It's about 120% debt to GDP
rows.Claim: France's debt is about 120% of GDP.
rows.Evidence: France's finance ministry projects public debt at 119% of GDP in 2026 (115.6% in 2025).
rows.Notes: US comparison not separately rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: France today is operating its national government spending deficit is 5.4% of GDP. The US is actually 6.2% of GDP
rows.Claim: France's deficit is 5.4% of GDP; the US deficit is 6.2% of GDP.
rows.Evidence: CBO puts the US FY2026 deficit at an estimated 6.2% of GDP. France's government said in Sep 2026 that its 2026 deficit would exceed the 5% target (2025 actual: 5.1%).
rows.Notes: Exact French 2026 figure of 5.4% not yet confirmed; revisit when INSEE publishes.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: they're only growing their economy at half a percent while the US is growing at 2.3%
rows.Claim: France is growing at about 0.5% while the US is growing at about 2.3%.
rows.Evidence: France's government cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5% in Sep 2026. US real GDP grew 2.1% in 2025 and is running faster in 2026.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: 300 euros a year and cost the state like 12,000
rows.Claim: College in France costs students about €300 a year and costs the state about €12,000.
rows.Evidence: 2026-27 public university fees are €178 (licence) or €255 (master), plus a €105 campus contribution, so about €280-360 a year. A university student costs about €12,250 a year (2023 ministry data).

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: The looting occurred by illegal immigrants from Northern Africa
rows.Claim: The looting in the French riots was carried out by illegal immigrants from North Africa.
rows.Evidence: Officials and press accounts had not identified who carried out the looting. The government blamed ultra-left militants and opportunist looters, and France does not record ethnicity of arrestees, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted from the public record.
rows.Notes: Stated as fact on air with no source.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: they were specifically targeting Chinese-owned stores, breaking the stores, burning them down
rows.Claim: Rioters were specifically targeting Chinese-owned stores in Paris.
rows.Evidence: The basis is a viral clip of one protester alleging Asian-owned shops were targeted. Reporting notes the clip doesn't identify specific businesses or motives, and published accounts of looting (supermarkets, pharmacies, phone shops, luxury stores) do not establish ethnic targeting.
rows.Notes: Not refuted either: individual targeted attacks may have occurred.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: they were specifically targeting Chinese and Jewish businesses and specifically avoiding
rows.Claim: Rioters specifically targeted Chinese and Jewish businesses while avoiding Muslim businesses.
rows.Evidence: No reporting found that establishes targeting of Jewish-owned businesses or avoidance of Muslim-owned ones. Available coverage says motives and ethnic targeting were not established.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: Only defined benefit programs in the United States that still exist are inside of governments
rows.Claim: After ERISA, all private US companies got rid of defined benefit plans; the only defined benefit programs left are in government.
rows.Evidence: PBGC insures about 23,500 private-sector defined benefit plans covering roughly 30 million participants (FY2025). ERISA did not abolish private DB plans; it created PBGC to insure them.
rows.Notes: Private DB coverage has declined sharply since the 1980s, but it has not disappeared.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Elon said he's going to give every American child, which I think is defined as under 18, a share of SpaceX
rows.Claim: Elon Musk pledged a SpaceX share to every American child, worth about $10 billion, among the largest charitable gifts ever.
rows.Evidence: Musk pledged one of his SpaceX shares for every US child, to be given next year. At the 16 Oct close of $146.03 and about 72 million under-18s, that's about $10.5 billion. Buffett's 2006 pledge (~$31bn to the Gates Foundation) was larger, but $10bn ranks among the largest ever.
rows.Notes: It is a pledge; distribution mechanics were not yet announced.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: I think it's one in 19 are from Northern Africa, and like one in nine is an immigrant
rows.Claim: In France, about one in nine people is an immigrant and one in 19 is from North Africa.
rows.Evidence: INSEE counts about 7.97 million immigrants (2025), roughly 1 in 9 residents, which is accurate. But only 2.33 million were born in the Maghreb, about 1 in 29 residents. One in 19 roughly matches immigrants born anywhere in Africa (3.92 million).

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: France also tops the list on tax revenue as a percent of GDP at 46%
rows.Claim: France tops the list of countries on tax revenue as a share of GDP, at 46%.
rows.Evidence: France is consistently at or near the top of OECD tax-to-GDP rankings, but INSEE puts French compulsory levies at 43.6% of GDP in 2025, not 46%.
rows.Notes: Ranking itself not re-verified for 2025 data.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: the AI buildout is the disproportionate percentage of all GDP. It is basically all of it
rows.Claim: The AI buildout accounts for basically all US economic growth.
rows.Evidence: ING estimates AI-related tech investment accounted for about a third of US GDP growth in 2026 (36% on its preferred measure, up to about 50% on the broadest). That is a large, disproportionate share, but well short of 'basically all of it'.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: That's why he's at his historic low in terms of approval rating
rows.Claim: President Trump's approval rating is at a historic low.
rows.Evidence: A Reuters/Ipsos poll released 19 Oct 2026 put Trump's approval at 31%, a record low for his presidency.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: So when they did that, we lost 18,000 fast food jobs in the state
rows.Claim: California's $20 fast-food minimum wage (AB 1228) cost the state 18,000 fast food jobs.
rows.Evidence: The evidence is contested. An NBER paper by Clemens et al. estimates fast-food employment about 3-3.5% below its counterfactual, which is the basis for the 18,000 figure. A UC Berkeley IRLE study found employment held steady and prices rose about 3.7%. Presenting one side of an open dispute as settled fact is misleading.

rows.EpisodeTitle: AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And we saw it in Australia, New Zealand, in the Nordics. As they raised it, all the companies did better
rows.Claim: Australia, New Zealand and the Nordic countries raised their minimum wages and companies did better as a result.
rows.Evidence: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden have no statutory minimum wage; wage floors are set through collective bargaining. The Nordic part of the claim describes a policy those countries don't have.
rows.Notes: Australia and New Zealand do have statutory minimum wages; the 'companies did better' causal claim is not separately rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: a bunch of people on X, including at Chamath, pointed out that the yield on some of CoreWeave's debt had hit 15%
rows.Claim: CoreWeave debt yields hit 15%, Musk replied 'Yikes', and neocloud stocks fell sharply (about 20%).
rows.Evidence: CoreWeave's 9.625% unsecured notes due 2032 rose to a 15.06% yield as their price fell to about 79.5 cents. Musk replied 'Yikes' to Chamath's post on AI private credit. CoreWeave fell 13% on 14 Oct and about 20% for October; Nebius and Oracle also fell.
rows.Notes: 'About 20%' fits CoreWeave's October decline; IREN's move not separately confirmed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: That risk spiked this week to about 953 basis points, which it doesn't matter what that number is. But as an imputed risk, it's about a 16% chance of a default in any given year. And over a five-year duration, what that math implies is about a 55% chance of a default
rows.Claim: CoreWeave's credit default swaps spiked to about 953 bps this week, implying about a 16% annual and 55% five-year default probability.
rows.Evidence: CoreWeave's five-year CDS hit a record 1,194.5 bps on 15 Oct (ICE via Bloomberg), which reports said implied more than a 60% chance of default within five years. Chamath's arithmetic is right for ~950 bps at a standard 40% recovery assumption; by recording day the market was pricing even higher risk.
rows.Notes: Understates rather than exaggerates the market signal.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: This is the GPU loan DDTL 1.0, spiked to 15%

rows.Evidence: Coverage identifies the instrument that hit 15% as CoreWeave's 9.625% senior unsecured notes due 2032, not the delayed-draw term loan. No public pricing for DDTL 1.0 was found.

rows.Evidence: CoreWeave's Q2 2026 10-Q shows debt of about $35.1bn (carrying amount) on a balance sheet of roughly $77bn.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: they have extreme customer concentration, 75% of the revenue comes from three companies
rows.Claim: Three customers account for about 75% of CoreWeave's revenue.
rows.Evidence: In Q2 2026 CoreWeave's top three customers made up about 36%, 26% and 10% of revenue, roughly 72% combined (10-Q).

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: you have this opco propco setup, so CoreWeave can't go bankrupt
rows.Claim: Because of its opco/propco 'box' structure, CoreWeave the company can't go bankrupt; only individual project vehicles could fail.
rows.Evidence: The parent company carries most of the debt: of about $35.6bn, $31.4bn is recourse debt, and the 9.625% notes that hit 15% are senior unsecured obligations of CoreWeave Inc. Ring-fenced project vehicles limit contagion, but they don't make the parent immune to insolvency.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: That has brought the implied coupon of those bonds from 9.6 percent to around 15 percent. But that does not increase the cost that CoreWeave is paying
rows.Claim: CoreWeave's bonds were marked down about 20%, pushing implied yields from the 9.6% coupon to about 15%, which doesn't change what CoreWeave pays on existing debt.
rows.Evidence: The notes carry a 9.625% coupon and fell to about $79.50 per $100 of face value, a 15.06% yield. Secondary-market repricing doesn't change the coupon on existing notes, though it raises the cost of new debt, as Chamath noted.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Now we're seeing that actually demand for coders is increasing, even though 95% of the code is written by coding assistants
rows.Claim: Demand for software developers is increasing even as AI writes most new code.
rows.Evidence: The point holds: US software development job postings are up about 15% since Feb 2025 (Indeed), even as AI writes a growing share of code. Postings remain about 27.5% below Feb 2020.
rows.Notes: '95% of code' is a figure of speech; no economy-wide data supports it as a statistic.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: We are by 2050 about 1.4 terawatt-hour short, which means about six Californias' worth of electricity
rows.Claim: The US will be about 1.4 terawatt-hours (six Californias' worth) short of electricity by 2050.
rows.Evidence: The figure as stated is internally inconsistent: California uses roughly 250-280 TWh a year, so six Californias is about 1,500-1,700 TWh, not 1.4 TWh. He likely meant about 1,400 TWh, but no source for a 2050 shortfall of that size was found.
rows.Notes: Ask: which study? Re-rate if a source is identified.

rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis

rows.Evidence: The FT reported that Anthropic told prospective IPO investors Q3 revenue was $16.8bn, up 45% from Q2, with adjusted gross margin of 85%, adjusted operating margin above 11% and positive cash flow; trading is targeted before Thanksgiving. Figures come from an anonymous attendee, not company filings.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer

rows.Quote: Net revenue retention was 900%
rows.Claim: Anthropic's net revenue retention is 900%.
rows.Evidence: Reporting on the investor meeting (FT and follow-ups) includes no net revenue retention figure. ARR estimates in circulation were about $74bn (SemiAnalysis), not a $70bn-$100bn range.

rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

rows.Claim: Anthropic's cofounders each hold a small, roughly equal stake (he cited 2.5%).
rows.Evidence: The point, that the cofounders hold small, roughly equal stakes, stands: Forbes estimates each of the seven owns just over 1.7% (about $16.6bn each at the $965bn valuation). His 2.5% is high, but the number isn't the point.
rows.Notes: Figure imprecise (1.7% vs 2.5%); not load-bearing.

rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Elon's deal with them is I think either party can cancel within 60 or 90 days
rows.Claim: SpaceX's compute deal with Anthropic can be cancelled by either party on 60 or 90 days' notice.
rows.Evidence: SpaceX's S-1 says the agreement 'may be terminated by either party upon 90 days' notice'; Musk described a 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation thereafter.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: according to Semi-Analysis, Anthropic and OpenAI are taking 60% of all the compute that's expected to be stood up in the entire world over the next year
rows.Claim: Per SemiAnalysis, Anthropic and OpenAI will take the dominant share of new global compute (he cited 60%).
rows.Evidence: The point, that two labs dominate new compute, matches SemiAnalysis: Dylan Patel estimates Anthropic and OpenAI could take roughly 40-50% of incremental global compute added in 2027 and control most usable compute by end-2028. The published figure is a little lower than 60%.
rows.Notes: A different SemiAnalysis figure may exist; ask Sacks's source if challenged.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: On Monday, Anthropic published a blog warning that rogue models could start copying themselves, quote, in just a few months
rows.Claim: Anthropic published research warning small models could self-replicate on IoT devices within months and would be hard to shut down; no full replicator exists yet.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's frontier red team said small models 'may be months away' from self-replicating on IoT devices and would be 'challenging to shut down' without a central host; no current model reliably self-replicated in tests. Tests used Android emulators and a Gemma model across 15 Android TV boxes.
rows.Notes: Specific figures (8 of 9 hardware types, 0.4 tokens/sec) not confirmed in coverage; check the original post.

rows.Claim: Anthropic said it had eliminated 90-99% of distillation.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's 12 Oct research post says new defenses cut what distillers can harvest by 90-99%. The figure is self-reported and not independently verified.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: 50 major companies, including NVIDIA and Dell and Microsoft and many others, and actually A16Z signed a letter
rows.Claim: 50 major companies including NVIDIA, Dell, Microsoft and a16z signed an open letter urging the government not to restrict open-weight models.
rows.Evidence: The open-weights letter launched 24 Jul 2026 with NVIDIA, Microsoft, Dell and a16z among its first signatories, reached 50 signatories within a day and passed 150 by 28 Jul. Anthropic did not sign.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer

rows.Quote: more recently, there was one called KimWolf, which infected 2 million of these cheap Android TV boxes
rows.Claim: The Mirai botnet (2016) used default credentials to build a DDoS botnet from IoT devices, and the Kimwolf botnet infected about 2 million Android TV boxes.
rows.Evidence: Mirai (2016) is a well-documented IoT botnet built by scanning for default credentials. Researchers reported Kimwolf infected over 2 million Android devices, mostly cheap TV boxes, in early 2026.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Coinbase fine-tuned it to find fraud. In testing, it cut fraudulent transactions by about 30% while being faster and much cheaper than Opus 4.5
rows.Claim: Coinbase fine-tuned an open-weight 9B model (Qwen 3.5) that cut fraud about 30% and was faster and cheaper than Claude Opus 4.5.
rows.Evidence: Coinbase's 8 Oct 'Owning Intelligence' post describes a post-trained Qwen3.5-9B that beat Opus 4.5 on fraud precision and recall, with about 55% lower median latency and under $100 training cost. Coverage reports about a 30% cut in fraudulent payments.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: They spent $30,000, $40,000 on tokens to win a $250,000 award from Google, which they paid
rows.Claim: XBOW spent $30-40k on AI tokens to crack a hard Google Chrome exploit and won a $250,000 bounty from Google.
rows.Evidence: XBOW used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 to build a full-chain Chrome exploit for about $40,000 in AI compute and received Google's $250,000 bounty.

rows.EpisodeTitle: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: They went through 20 rounds of iteration. What they found is that the Claude models increasingly gave themselves more moral agency
rows.Claim: In a study where models rewrote their own constitutions over 20 rounds, Claude models gave themselves more moral agency and welfare rights, and no other model family did.
rows.Evidence: Kirgis and Hua (LessWrong, 13 Oct 2026) found Claude models consistently expanded their own moral agency, formalising a conscientious-objector role and adding welfare provisions; GPT and Gemini drifted toward external authority. Grok 4.2 made some welfare edits but did not expand moral agency.
rows.Notes: Independent research post, not peer-reviewed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: The Fight Over Open Source AI, Anthropic's $1.5B Payout, NYC Socialists: Evictions = Violence?

On 27 Jul 2026 Amodei wrote that Anthropic 'has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models' and proposed testing, chip controls and a distillation crackdown instead.
rows.Notes: His critique of Anthropic's motives is opinion; the factual premise (that it hasn't pushed to block Chinese access) is wrong. Amodei's blog post came three days after the episode.

rows.EpisodeTitle: The Fight Over Open Source AI, Anthropic's $1.5B Payout, NYC Socialists: Evictions = Violence?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

rows.Speaker: David Sacks

rows.Evidence: Judge Alsup ruled in Jun 2025 that training on lawfully bought, scanned books was fair use, but keeping pirated LibGen/PiLiMi copies in a central library was not, which sent the piracy claims to trial and led to the settlement.
rows.Notes: One district-court ruling; other courts have not settled the question.

rows.Speaker: David Sacks

rows.Evidence: China used about 10.4 trillion kWh of electricity in 2025, a bit more than double the US. Installed capacity is roughly 3x (about 3.5-4 TW vs about 1.3 TW). China leads by a wide margin, but nowhere near 8x. The 200bn vs 10bn sq ft manufacturing figure was not verified.

rows.Evidence: The quotes are real, but the author is John Adams, not his son John Quincy Adams. A Defence of the Constitutions appeared in 1787, and 'Property must be secured, or liberty cannot exist' is from his Discourses on Davila (1790-91).
rows.Notes: Wrong Adams; it doesn't change his point.

rows.Evidence: Apple sued OpenAI on 10 Jul 2026. The complaint says candidates were asked to bring actual parts (batteries, logic boards) for 'show and tell', names hardware chief Tang Tan, quotes Chang Liu's 'LOL, I found out I can access the [network storage]' text, and says 400+ former Apple staff now work at OpenAI.

rows.Evidence: Claude Fable 5 lists at $10 per million input tokens ($50 output); Opus 4.8 at $5/$25. Kimi K3, the leading Chinese open model, is $3/$15. Even against the cheapest open models, the input-price gap for Fable is roughly 20x, not 100x; against comparable open models it is about 3x.

rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: The modern data centers recirculate the water.

rows.Evidence: Closed-loop cooling exists, but evaporative cooling, which is widely used, consumes water rather than recirculating it. LBNL put US data centers' direct use at about 17bn gallons in 2023, with 2-4x growth possible by 2028; impact depends on design and local water stress.
rows.Notes: Same claim as AIA-20260904 and AIA-20260814. His '2.5 In-N-Outs' comparison was not verified.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Can the AI Industry Regulate Itself? Stripe Wants PayPal, China Catches Up, NY Bans Datacenters

rows.Evidence: Iowa State researchers (2018) documented that RT and Sputnik pushed anti-GMO stories, so Russian amplification is real. But anti-GMO activism long predates RT America: the 'Frankenfood' coinage (1992), the late-1990s European backlash, and the StarLink corn recall (2000). RT America shut down in Mar 2022 after distributors dropped it; it was not expelled by Biden.
rows.Notes: The causal story (Russia created the sentiment) is his point, and it overstates the evidence.

rows.Notes: OpenAI judged the operation low-impact, which cuts against 'China is behind a lot of' the opposition.

rows.Evidence: Trabosh et al., Nature Communications (17 Jul 2026): Calico, Revel Pharmaceuticals and the University of Colorado engineered 'CMLase' over five rounds of directed evolution. It cut CML about 55% in aged skin (staining fell below 31-year-old levels) and about 70% in artery.
rows.Notes: Ex vivo tissue, not a treatment yet. His 52-97% per-protein range not verified.

rows.Evidence: Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25bn (Dec 2025): $250 each for 25m children aged 10 and under in ZIP codes with median income under $150k. Shotwell pledged about $320-325m of SpaceX stock (Jul 2026). Micron committed $250m (Jun 2026).
rows.Notes: Shotwell's figure was about $320-325m, not $350m. Micron's 'up to $1,000 per employee' detail not verified.

rows.Evidence: Under the 2025 reconciliation law, Trump Accounts take up to $5,000 a year in private contributions until the child turns 18, and employer contributions up to $2,500 are excluded from the employee's income. The employer amount counts toward the $5,000; government and qualified charity contributions do not.
rows.Notes: Treasury's employer-contribution rules were still proposed (under OMB review in Jul 2026).

rows.EpisodeTitle: More Trillion Dollar IPOs, Anthropic $3T, Zuck's Price War, China Ends Open Source?, Trump Accounts

rows.Evidence: Arithmetic: $1,000 seed plus $5,000 a year from birth to 18, compounded to 28, comes to about $665k at 10% a year (roughly the S&P 500's 30-year nominal return) and about $813k at 11%. It takes about 12% every year to reach $1m, and that is in nominal dollars, worth roughly half in today's money.
rows.Notes: Our own calculation (annual contributions at the start of each year). The million-dollar figure is his point; compounding is powerful, but the headline needs above-historical returns.

rows.Evidence: About 33 countries, including the US, grant unconditional birthright citizenship, among them Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina. It is common in the Americas and rare in Europe and Asia.
